choices: It queries each router's management interface
It sends packets with incrementing TTL values; each router that decrements TTL to zero returns ICMP Time Exceeded, revealing itself
It reads the routing table of the destination
explanation: Each router identifies itself purely as a side effect of the loop-prevention mechanism. Implementations differ — classic Unix uses UDP to high ports, Windows uses ICMP Echo, and -T uses TCP SYN, which is often the only variant that gets through a firewall.
